The Long Walk Home

By A. Fixture Author

The road out of the valley was longer than the maps admitted, and the walkers knew it by the second afternoon. They kept a slow pace and counted the fence posts, because counting was easier than thinking about the miles that remained ahead of them on the winding gravel track.

By evening the ridge line had flattened into a smudge of blue, and the village lights came up one by one, each a small argument against the dark. Nobody spoke for the last mile; there was nothing left to say that the road had not already said for them.

What the walk taught

Distance is honest. It does not care what the map promised, and it decides every argument between hope and geography in geography's favour, every single time, without malice and without exception.

  • Carry less than you think you need.
  • Count fence posts, not miles.
